pos.personaBrief: Dynamo valued possession but adapted: sat deeper against Bayern to counter, Blokhin sent away in quick transitions; rated dominance by danger created.

pro.personaBrief: Quick transitions and few-touch attacks after winning the ball, Blokhin in behind; yet libero Konkov was tasked with starting attacks, so build-up was not purely long.

est.personaBrief: Interchanging movement and universalism (Onyshchenko, Buryak behind Blokhin; varied readings of the system) within a rehearsed scientific framework.

lar.personaBrief: Full-backs Troshkin and Matvienko pushed forward at pace and Blokhin ran the left, but the attack was built around a central trio behind a lone striker.

blo.personaBrief: Pressed from the off in the final, forwards cut passing lanes starting from Blokhin and Onyshchenko; sat deeper only against Bayern as an adaptation.

mar.personaBrief: Collective pressing that cuts passing lanes and covers space; no man-marking label found, so leaning to space and lane coverage.

pla.personaBrief: Lobanovskyi imposed a scientific model but adapted match by match (sat deeper vs Bayern, dialectic of counter-play).

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic and results-driven: won the Cup Winners' Cup and Super Cup, saw out Bayern 1-0 away with instructions to drop back.

sis.personaBrief: Collective system with computerised testing and universal duties for all; stars like Blokhin pressed and worked within roles.

jog.personaBrief: Midfield combined skill with ceaseless running; physical intensity was a base requirement, with technique in the fabric of the team.

bas.personaBrief: Squad of 12-13 national team regulars in their prime, young coaches, mix of age; built via signings from Ukraine and elsewhere, not academy-centred.

lid.personaBrief: Lobanovskyi as strict boss with rules for all, though reassuring players personally; authority over harmony.
